title: Ranveer Singh Is Making India's First Zombie Epic. It Costs ₹300 Crore and Starts Shooting Next Month.
excerpt: Pralay pairs the Dhurandhar megastar with Malayalam sensation Kalyani Priyadarshan for a post-apocalyptic survival thriller that aims to rewrite what Indian cinema can look like.
body:
There is a version of Bollywood that plays it safe — rom-coms, sequels, the occasional biopic with a flag in the background. And then there is whatever **Ranveer Singh** is doing right now.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=7WGn4xSSL2M</youtube>

Fresh off the most dominant box office run in Indian cinema history — **Dhurandhar 2: The Revenge** crossed ₹1,800 crore worldwide and is still selling tickets in its eleventh week — Singh has locked in his next move. And it is, to put it mildly, unhinged.

**Pralay**, directed by first-time feature filmmaker **Jai Mehta**, is a post-apocalyptic zombie thriller set in a devastated Mumbai. The reported budget is ₹300 crore. Principal photography begins in August 2026. And the leading lady is **Kalyani Priyadarshan**, the Malayalam actress who turned heads in **Lokah** and is now making her Hindi debut opposite the biggest male star in the country.

Singh reportedly convinced Kalyani personally. According to Sacnilk, he reached out directly after watching her work in South Indian cinema, believing she had the raw intensity the role demanded. That kind of casting — skipping the usual Bollywood shortlist to pull someone from a completely different industry — tells you everything about where Pralay is headed.

## A Genre India Has Never Touched

Let's be honest: Indian cinema has flirted with horror, dabbled in sci-fi, and occasionally gestured toward the apocalyptic. But a full-scale zombie survival thriller? With AI-driven visual effects, physical sets built to simulate urban collapse, and a tone that the makers compare to **World War Z** and **I Am Legend**? That has simply never been attempted.

The story follows a man fighting to protect his family as Mumbai transforms into a wasteland — part survival drama, part creature feature, part love story told under impossible circumstances. **Hanshal Mehta**, Jai's father and one of Indian cinema's most respected filmmakers, has been vocal about the project's ambitions. When rumors circulated that Pralay was an adaptation of José Saramago's novel *Blindness*, Hanshal shut them down firmly: this is an original screenplay, developed by Jai and co-writer **Vishal Kapoor**.

> "A novel like Blindness is not easily adapted to film. Pralay is its own beast." — Hanshal Mehta

The production plans to merge physical sets with cutting-edge AI-driven visuals to create a dystopian atmosphere unlike anything seen in Indian cinema. Think crumbling skylines, overrun streets, and the kind of large-scale destruction that Hollywood usually reserves for $200 million tentpoles.

## The Don 3 Shadow

Pralay also arrives against a complicated backdrop. Singh's exit from **Don 3** — the Farhan Akhtar-directed sequel that had already invested heavily in pre-production — triggered a non-cooperation directive from FWICE and a legal battle that is still unfolding. The actor has filed suit against the federation, challenging the legitimacy of their directive.

But if Pralay is Ranveer's answer to the controversy, it is a spectacular one. Rather than retreating into something commercial and comfortable, he is doubling down on ambition — a genre-defining project with a debut director, an unconventional leading lady, and a budget that signals absolute conviction.

## Why Diaspora Audiences Should Pay Attention

For NRIs who have grown up on Hollywood zombie lore — **The Walking Dead**, **28 Days Later**, **Train to Busan** — Pralay represents something genuinely new: that same survival-horror adrenaline, but filtered through an Indian sensibility. A Mumbai setting. A family drama at its core. A star who has proven he can carry spectacle and emotion simultaneously.

Kalyani Priyadarshan, meanwhile, brings something Bollywood's current roster of leading ladies often lacks: genuine unpredictability. Her Malayalam work has a stillness and ferocity that could make her a breakout in Hindi cinema, especially paired with Ranveer's volcanic energy.

The film is produced by **True Story Films** in association with Ranveer's own **Ma Kasam Films**. No release date has been announced, but with an August 2026 shoot start and the VFX-heavy post-production that a project like this demands, a late 2027 release window feels most likely.

Bollywood has been talking about genre-breaking for years. Pralay might actually mean it.
